classification.habit: Erect perennial herb, 1–2 m tall, arising from paired tuberous roots.
classification.habitat: Alpine and sub-alpine meadows and scrub of the Himalaya, about 3,000–5,000 m.
classification.distribution: Temperate and alpine Himalaya: Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Nepal.

identification.description: Conical tuberous root resembling a calf's navel, dark brown exterior with longitudinal wrinkles, whitish or pinkish internal fracture; highly toxic in unpurified state.
identification.whole_plant: Tall erect herb with deeply palmately divided leaves and a terminal raceme of blue to purple helmet-shaped flowers, from paired dark tubers.
identification.root: Paired, ovoid-conical tuberous roots tapering to a point, 2–4.5 cm long and 0.4–1.8 cm thick, wrinkled, dark brown to blackish-brown with root scars; fracture cartilaginous, white within the cambium ring; taste slightly bitter followed by strong tingling and numbness; poisonous (API).
identification.stem: Erect, stout, unbranched or sparsely branched leafy stem.
identification.leaf: Alternate, long-petioled leaves, palmately deeply divided into 3–5 lobed and toothed segments.
identification.flower: Zygomorphic, blue to purple flowers in terminal racemes; the upper sepal forms a hood or helmet.
identification.seed: Many small, angular or winged seeds.
identification_points: Conical tuberous root resembling a calf's navel, dark brown exterior with longitudinal wrinkles, whitish or pinkish internal fracture; highly toxic in unpurified state.

therapeutics.dose: 15–30 mg (shodhita only; API) — after shodhana only
therapeutics.precautions: Highly poisonous Sthavara visha (Kanda visha). Use internally ONLY after classical shodhana (gomutra bhavana for 3 days, or Dola yantra swedana in gomutra or godugdha) and only in the API dose of 15–30 mg of shodhita drug, almost always within a formulation. Exceeding the dose is dangerous. Ashodhita Vatsanabha, even in small amounts, can cause tingling and numbness of mouth and limbs, vomiting, hypotension, arrhythmias and death. To be prescribed only by a qualified physician; never for self-medication.
therapeutics.contraindications: Ashodhita (unpurified) drug in any form; pregnancy and lactation; children and the elderly or debilitated; heart disease, arrhythmias or hypotension; Pitta-predominant conditions, Raktapitta and Daha; hot season and use with heat exposure; patients with poor Agni or debility; long-term use.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Toxicity is due to C19-diterpenoid ester alkaloids such as aconitine and pseudaconitine, which keep sodium channels open; shodhana partly hydrolyses them to far less toxic benzoyl derivatives.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Processed aconite, used in fevers, pain and digestion.
recognized_uses: Ingredient of classical Rasaushadhis for fever and pain in very small doses
No safe use outside qualified practice
modern_information.safety_notes: Aconite poisoning causes oral and limb paresthesia, vomiting, hypotension, ventricular arrhythmias and can be fatal; there is no specific antidote. Raw roots must never be consumed.

exam_points: Botanical name: Aconitum ferox Wall. ex Ser. (API monograph: A. chasmanthum); Family: Ranunculaceae
Rasa: Madhura; Guna: Laghu, Ruksha, Tikshna, Vikasi, Vyavayi; Virya: Ushna
Karma: Yogavahi, Jwarahara, Swedana, Vedanasthapana, Rasayana (after shodhana)
Sthavara Kanda visha; shodhana in gomutra is mandatory
Formulations: Tribhuvanakirti Rasa, Anandabhairava Rasa, Mahavishagarbha Taila

doctor.quick_reference: Vatsanabha is a Sthavara visha used only after shodhana, 15–30 mg, mostly inside Rasaushadhis for Jwara, Vatavyadhi and pain; ashodhita drug or overdose can be fatal.
doctor.dose: 15–30 mg (shodhita only; API) — after shodhana only
key_precautions: Shodhana is mandatory before internal use
Never exceed 15–30 mg of shodhita drug
Avoid in pregnancy, children, heart disease and Pitta conditions
Monitor for tingling, vomiting, hypotension and arrhythmia
Prescription by a qualified physician only
